newsitem.title: USA: CBOT CORN ENDS UP 12-CENT LIMIT ON USDA CROP DATA.
newsitem.headline: CBOT CORN ENDS UP 12-CENT LIMIT ON USDA CROP DATA.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed up their 12-cent limit in most months, triggering expanded 18-cent limits Wednesday, on today's bullish USDA August crop production report, traders said.

"Clearly the influence in corn was the crop report being much lower than expected and on top of that the decline in crop conditions," said Smith Barney analyst Dale Gustafson. "We'll probably be limit up tomorrow and maybe Thursday the market will get to where it wants to go."

USDA Tuesday estimated 1997 U.S. corn production at 9.276 billion bushels, sharply below the July USDA World Board forecast for 9.7 billion and below an average of analysts' estimates for 9.554 billion bushels. The forecast was below the lowest analyst estimate at 9.375 billion.

Traders said there was a buying pool in corn futures of roughly 110 million bushels with 75 million bushels wanted in the December contract. In corn options, the synthetic for December was traded at roughly $2.74 which would indicate an eleven cent per bushel higher open Wednesday.
Corn closed up four cents to the limit, with September 12 cents higher at $2.61-3/4 per bushel and December up the same at $2.65-1/4.
Traders said the corn market also was boosted by a cut by USDA to 110 million tonnes from the previous 122 million tonnes in its estimate for China's corn crop.

The market also found support from Monday's USDA weekly state crop briefs which showed the U.S. corn as of Sunday at 58 percent good to excellent, below the 66 percent in that category the previous week.
Reports of only scattered rainfall so far this week in central Illinois also was cited as a supportive influence.

A few scattered thunderstorms swept across the driest area of west central Illinois Monday night but the coverage was not that high, said Weather Services Corp senior agricultural meteorologist Joel Burgio.
Cargill Inc sold five million bushels of December and bought two million December and ADM Investor Services sold one half million bushels of December, traders said.
In spread dealings, Tenco Inc did two million bushels of March/December at 7-1/2 to 7-1/4 cents, premium March, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 30,000 contracts, below the 53,688 traded Monday.
In corn options, Refco Inc bought 4,000 December $1.90 calls at 83 to 85-1/2 cents and Cargill Investor Services sold 2,500 December $1.90 calls at 83 to 85-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 35,000 contracts, above the 21,280 traded Monday.
